gaps.sentence: The temple is thought ___ (build) more than two thousand years ago.
gaps.explanation: Perfect passive infinitive: to have been + built for an event earlier than the main verb.

gaps.sentence: The recipe ___ (pass down) from generation to generation.
gaps.hint: continuing relevance from past to now
gaps.explanation: Present perfect passive: has been + passed down; the process links past and present.

gaps.sentence: Too much time ___ (waste) on pointless meetings these days.
gaps.explanation: 'These days' signals a present general situation: is + wasted (singular 'time').

gaps.sentence: A cheaper version of the vaccine ___ right now.
gaps.explanation: 'Right now' requires present continuous passive: is being + developed.

gaps.sentence: The stage was still wet — the scenery ___ (paint) only hours before.
gaps.explanation: 'Only hours before' points to the past perfect passive: had been + painted.

gaps.sentence: Nothing ___ about the incident until the inquiry began.
gaps.explanation: Nothing was known by anybody: past simple passive was + known.

gaps.sentence: The suspect is believed ___ the country weeks ago.
gaps.explanation: Believe + to-infinitive; 'weeks ago' demands the perfect infinitive to have left.

gaps.sentence: He's getting his eyes ___ next week.
gaps.explanation: Causative get + object + past participle: getting his eyes tested (by an optician).
